item.title: Atlanta Jazz Festival is turning 49, announces 2026 lineup
item.description: The Atlanta Jazz Festival has announced its lineup for its 49th annual event, featuring Atlanta-based artists, Grammy-winning musicians, and internationally recognized performers, and will be held in Piedmont Park over Memorial Day weekend. The post Atlanta Jazz Festival is turning 49, announces 2026 lineup appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: J. Alexander’s coming to The Battery, looking to hire nearly 100 staffers
item.description: J. Alexander's is opening a new location at The Battery in Cobb County, Georgia, and is looking to hire 90-100 front and back-of-house positions to provide dining options for Atlanta Braves and Major League Baseball fans. The post J. Alexander’s coming to The Battery, looking to hire nearly 100 staffers appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: In Georgia’s “Original Vision,” a 21st Century Call to Action
item.description: Georgia's founders envisioned the state as an experiment in economic development and social welfare reform, but despite its success as a business hub, the state still ranks low in quality of life metrics such as cost of living, child well-being, and access to healthcare. The post In Georgia’s “Original Vision,” a 21st Century Call to Action appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: Educator Astrid Ross announces candidacy for Georgia State Senate District 7
item.description: Astrid Ross, a long-term Gwinnett educator and mental health advocate, is running for Georgia State Senate District 7 to help sustain the district as a good place to raise a family by advocating for educational funding and mental health resources. The post Educator Astrid Ross announces candidacy for Georgia State Senate District 7 appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: ‘Atlanta shows up for Atlanta’: City declares Feb. 12 Kenan Thompson Day
item.description: Kenan Thompson, the longest-tenured cast member in "Saturday Night Live" history, was honored by the City of Atlanta with a proclamation declaring February 12, 2026, as "Kenan Thompson Day" in recognition of his Atlanta roots and his contributions to the city's culture. The post ‘Atlanta shows up for Atlanta’: City declares Feb. 12 Kenan Thompson Day appeared first on The Atlanta Voice.

item.title: When a Black Newspaper Goes Quiet
item.description: The closing of the Richmond Free Press marks more than the end of a newspaper. It marks the quieting of a civic institution. Founded in 1992 by Raymond H. Boone Sr., the Richmond Free Press was created to provide independent, accountable journalism for Black Richmond. Boone brought deep professional grounding to that mission. item.description: Bernard and Pamela Solomon, a couple married for nearly 34 years, have built a life rooted in faith, family, and service, and have now become franchise owners of AtWork in Forest Park. item.title: ‘Divas, Blues, and Memories’: Artist Chronicles LGBTQ History Through Button-Encrusted Art
item.description: "Beau McCall: Divas, Blues, and Memories" is an exhibition at the Hammonds House Museum that celebrates the healing power of music and the LGBTQ community, featuring button-encrusted collages that pay tribute to friends lost to AIDS and other social ills.
